newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek equities drop 4.65pct in panic selloff.
newsitem.headline: Greek equities drop 4.65pct in panic selloff.

text.p: Greek shares dropped 4.65 percent on Friday and market watchers said the capital market commission's statements on Wednesday had caused a chaotic situation in the Athens bourse.
On Wednesday, capital market commission president Stavros Thomadakis warned investors against speculation and rumour-based investment decisions.

"Thomadakis' warning was catalytic for the market. The bourse should have been left on its own to determine whether it was overvalued or undervalued," said George Politis, an analyst at Eurosec Securities.
Government and capital market officials should realise that the bourse's rise is very significant for the long-term economic growth of Greece, he said.
Everything was positive for Greek equities in 1997 -- the planned listing of the Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP), the flotation of another stake in OTE telecom and rights issues of several banks.
"No one should have interfered in that way, because the Greek bourse is shallow," he said.
"If state banks and brokerage houses intervene to control the fall, then we could see the market rebounding in the medium-term with a new support level at 1,200 points, he added.
Politis also said that foreign investors were afraid of a further market deterioration and were pulling funds out of Greek equities.
Another analyst said that the panic selling that started on Thursday and carried on through Friday's session was unreasonable.

"People were running like crazy, looking to sell after Thomadakis' statements. This is stupid, because there is no serious reason to exit the Greek bourse," said John Kannelopoulos, chief analyst at Aspis Securities.
He admitted market psychology had turned sour and if a similar fall continued, we could be faced with a "Black Monday."
The Athens general share index closed 4.65 percent down or 63.53 points lower at 1303.63 from Thursday's 1367.16, after opening at 1342.24.
Turnover was 28.5 billion drachmas on volume of 7.0 million shares. Decliners led advancers 199 to 29 with 20 issues unchanged on 248 issues traded.

Sectoral indices were down, with biggest losses incurred in construction and banking shares, down 5.51 and 7.70 percent respectively. Industrials lost 5.14 percent and small-caps ended 2.66 percent down.
Insurance stocks settled 3.37 percent lower, leasing shares ended 2.65 percent weaker and investment shares closed 1.79 percent down.
